¶ 4. forgotten lyres] An Aeolian harp could be left in a window or tree for the wind to make music.
 dissonant] variously-sounding. Cp. Coleridge’s ‘Eolian Harp’ (1796) 40–3: ‘. . . many idle flitting phan-
tasies,/Traverse my indolent and passive brain,/As wild and various as the random gales/That swell and
flutter on this subject Lute!’
 Man’s yesterday . . . his morrow] Cp. Ovid, Met. xv 215–16: ‘nec quod fuimusve sumusve,/cras
erimus’.
 Nought . . . Mutability] Cp. Spenser, FQ VII vii 47, lines 8–9: ‘Wherefore, this lower world who can
deny/But to be subject still to Mutabilitie?’
